accepted.message: Overly permissive mask in open sets file to group readable.
accepted.reason: Same release tree, same group: the staged files are created with the mode they will keep, so the open and the later chmod agree rather than leaving a window at a different mode. Covers two writes since 2026-09-06 (B103): the node artifact under node_path, and MANIFEST.json beside it. The manifest is not pulled by a node and needs no group read of its own, but it lives in the release tree and is owned like the rest of it - a file in that tree with a mode of its own would be the exception somebody has to remember.

accepted.message:
Insecure SSL/TLS protocol version TLSv1_1 allowed by [call to ssl.create_default_context](1).
Insecure SSL/TLS protocol version TLSv1 allowed by [call to ssl.create_default_context](1).
accepted.reason: TLS 1.0 is not reachable and the alert overstates by naming it: MIN_VERSIONS is an allowlist of exactly TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3, a target naming anything else is refused before a context exists, and minimum_version is always set explicitly rather than inherited from OpenSSL. What remains is that `legacy` floors at TLS 1.1, which is the feature B83 built for one named appliance on a network the operator owns - applied per target that asked for it and never to the rest of the request. The probe must not hold a floor of its own: HAProxy reaches the pool under the policy the object names, and a probe that refused what HAProxy accepts would report a healthy pool as broken.

accepted.message: Untrusted URL redirection depends on a [user-provided value](1).
accepted.reason: Three 303s that land on the registry row the button was pressed on (8632a06): resume_enrollment, publish_certificate and _queue_import's open_row (the import and renewal form). The value is a certificate ID and has passed config.CERTIFICATE_ID.fullmatch - ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,254}$ - before the redirect is built, through operations.prepare, which raises BadPayload on anything else and answers 400 before a job is queued. So it holds no slash, colon, question mark, ampersand, hash or newline, and it is appended to the fixed prefix '/certificates?view=registry&open=', so it cannot begin the target, become '//host', or add a second query parameter. CodeQL does not carry the allowlist check that far. Re-check every redirect here when CERTIFICATE_ID loosens, or when one appends the value to something other than a literal path. Moved from views.py with the certificate pages (K1, 2026-10-22); _queue_import's redirect had been covered by the views.py entry without being named in it.

accepted.message: Overly permissive mask in chmod sets file to group readable.
accepted.reason: The per-certificate directory a receiver fetches from (C7, B138). Group read and execute is what lets the receiver's own account reach the 0600 files inside it; the directory itself stays owned by root and not writable by the account, which is the point - a receiver reads what it was given and cannot replace it. The group is the account's own, created with it by haprion-cert-receiver, so group read reaches one receiver and no other. Re-check if a receiver account is ever given a shared group.

accepted.message: Overly permissive mask in chmod sets file to group readable.
accepted.reason: 2026-09-17: The directory a receiver fetches from, made 0750 root with the fetch account's own group. Group read and execute is how that one account reaches the 0600 files inside; root ownership is what stops it replacing them - the contract the publisher's per-certificate directory carries, decided in the same C7 pass. The second is B306's (2026-10-14): the directory an https receiver's user files live in, made 0750 root:www-data; nginx's workers run as www-data and read auth_basic_user_file on every request, the group reads and never writes. The files themselves are written through haprion.atomic_file since 2026-10-23 and no longer alerts here.

accepted.message: Overly permissive mask in chmod sets file to world readable.
accepted.reason: 2026-09-17: The fetch account's .ssh directory, made 0755 root-owned - B131's shape, proven on the node accounts in production: sshd reads the lock as root, and an account that owned or could write it could replace its own restrictions. Its authorized_keys and the sshd drop-in or nginx site the command writes (0644, root-owned, no secret) go through haprion.atomic_file since 2026-10-23 and are no longer alerts here.

accepted.reason: B306: the password an https receiver fetches with is made by this command and printed to the operator who ran it, once, because the receiver must be given it and the manager keeps only its hash. It is printed only when the operator passes --show-password, and the command refuses to make one without it; the interface is the ordinary way and shows it on the page instead. It goes to stdout of the operator's own terminal, never to a log, the audit trail or the registry.
